basics.name: Lorenzo Graizzaro
basics.label: Software Developer | AI Engineer
basics.summary: Software Developer focused on AI Engineering. I build full-stack applications with built-in AI: agents with Amazon Bedrock and Strands Agents, LLM generation, RAG, and MCP servers. Core stack: React, TypeScript, NestJS, Python/FastAPI, and Kotlin/Spring Boot, with SQL and NoSQL databases and serverless deployment on AWS. I work with Spec-Driven Development and agentic environments (Claude Code with subagents) to own architecture decisions.

skills.name: Cloud
keywords: AWS (Lambda, API Gateway, Bedrock, DynamoDB, S3, SQS, Cognito, Polly, Lightsail, AWS SAM)

projects.name: Prioria
projects.description: Android app that intercepts notifications, prioritizes them with an AI agent, and reads critical ones aloud. 100% serverless AWS backend.
highlights: Agent built with Strands Agents SDK and Amazon Bedrock that scores each notification against user rules and preferences, and learns from explicit feedback
Serverless backend on AWS Lambda, API Gateway, Cognito, DynamoDB, and SQS, defined as infrastructure as code with AWS SAM
Text-to-speech for critical notifications with Amazon Polly and a native Android widget

projects.name: StudyQuest
projects.description: Collaborative study platform with real-time matchmaking and AI-generated quizzes from notes and PDFs. Running in production on AWS.
highlights: LLM-powered quiz generation from PDF and DOCX files: Markdown conversion through a Python microservice (MarkItDown) and a pluggable AI provider (Amazon Bedrock by default, Google Gemini as fallback)
Hybrid persistence: PostgreSQL with TypeORM for metadata and results, DynamoDB with TTL for quiz content, and S3 with presigned URLs for files
Real-time matchmaking, study rooms, and chat over WebSockets (Socket.IO); NestJS API on AWS Lightsail with Docker Compose, Caddy (TLS), and least-privilege IAM
Changes specified with OpenSpec before implementation (Spec-Driven Development)

projects.name: OpenRuleta
projects.description: Self-hostable raffle toolkit for events: public sign-up form and an operator-facing winner wheel, built on Supabase.
highlights: Used live at Data Saturday LATAM Argentina 2026 with ~300 concurrent mobile sign-ups on Supabase's free tier
Security through Row Level Security: the public app can only insert; the operator wheel uses the service key behind HTTP Basic Auth

projects.name: FraudDetector
projects.description: Bank fraud detection over 100k+ transactions using a consensus of 3 unsupervised ML models and an interactive dashboard.
highlights: Ensemble of Isolation Forest, LOF, and K-Means: a client is flagged only when at least 2 models agree (~35% fewer false positives than a single model)
REST API with FastAPI: 110–150 ms per client analysis and 40–60 ms per transaction

projects.name: BookLibre
projects.description: Full-stack book reservation and rental system, group academic project (UNSAM).
highlights: Polyglot persistence with PostgreSQL, MongoDB, and Redis behind a Kotlin + Spring Boot backend
JWT authentication with HttpOnly cookies and SameSite=None for cross-origin sessions
